questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A study destination with English as it's first language, so people wouldn't have to speak a different language to include me in their conversations

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay. The website was pretty confusing at first, but at some point you learn how to find what you need.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: No assistance

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Both single and shared rooms. Some in halls and some in townhouses.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: When living in halls you mostly have limited access to a kitchen, but a meal plan is mandatory and there are several of places to eat at campus. In the townhouses you'll have a kitchen shared between 4-6 people.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
Most exchange students live in East Village, so if you want to live with fellow exchange students, that is the place to be.
West residence is a bit far from campus, but if you want peace it is a good place to be (there can be a lot of partying at East Village on the weekends).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I really liked to live in one of the townhouses in East Village. The kitchen is nice and you only share your bathroom with 1-2 people. 
Housing is pretty expensive, but it is so much easier to make new friends etc. when you stay at campus, so in my opinion it is worth the money.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I got an email saying that I just had to send an email to a specific professor telling them what courses I would like to take. The only confusing think was which courses counted as master's courses and which didn't. Senior undergraduate courses (course code 4000-4999) count as master's courses at UCPH even though they are undergraduate courses at UoG.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could email Mike Lafleur (Education Abroad Advisor) at any time and he would help me with my course registration.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Some courses are more popular than my courses, so make sure to have everthing settled (e.g. pre-approval) before course registration opens, so you are ready to apply as soon as it opens

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Even though I took Senior Undergraduate courses I think the level was pretty low compared to UCPH. We learned stuff here that I was taught at my first or second year at UCPH. However, they do have a lot of assignments etc. that all count towards your final grade, so even though the courses are easier you still have to use a lot of time doing the assignments etc.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Everything you do counts towards you final grade.
Also the teaching was slower (they spend more time explaining), so it was easier to follow along compared to at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Statistical Computing, Applied Multivariate Statistical Methods, Applied Time Series Analysis.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Statistical Computing is a very nice course where you get to use R a lot and the professor (Lorna Deeth) is very nice.
Applied Time Series Analysis is an interesting course, mainly because of the professor (Justin Slater) who is a very good teacher.

Housing DKK per month *

Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I did not need any books for my courses, so that was definitely less expensive than expected. However, I expected that food would be cheaper than I Denmark, but it turned out to be slightly more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There were a lot of activities available if you were living on campus. There also is a well-equipted fitness centre which is pretty cheap (around 300 DKK for one semester), where they also have a lot of classes (spinning, zumba, yoga etc.) and a swimming pool.
They also have an ice rink.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Zumba class with Steph (Stephanie Munger) is amazing <3

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Niagara Falls, Toronto and Algonquin national park

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. It is not that far from the Danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Thanksgiving/Halloween

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. The housing on campus is expensive but worth it.
2. If you are living in a townhouse, reach out to your roommates before moving in, to talk about who's bringing what to the kitchen. That way you won't have to buy a lot of stuff that you can't take home with you at the end of your stay.
3. Have fun! Make sure to go on trips on weekends. If you gather a group of other exchange students you can rent a car pretty cheap and get a place to stay through AirBnb.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember your bathing suit so you can use the indoor swimming pool!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the new friends I made

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being so far away from home for 4 months is a long time and I missed my family a lot towards the end of my stay. However, I am glad that I went on exchange and when I got home I felt like time just flew by at my exchange stay.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
